newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ business confidence sluggish - bank survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ business confidence sluggish - bank survey.

text.p: New Zealand business confidence remains disappointingly sluggish, National Bank of New Zealand Ltd said in its latest survey on Wednesday.
A net 11.8 percent of respondents expected an improvement in general business confidence over the next 12 months, up only slightly from seven percent in December.
"In general, however, business confidence appears to lack conviction, having floundered between minus 25 percent and 20 percent since mid-1996," NBNZ said.
"These levels have not been enough to sustain strong growth and investment, with the economy now well below its 1995 pace."

The overall outlook was positive but subdued. Further interest rate falls, signs of improved international economic activity and higher than expected growth in New Zealand since the last survey in December had been offset by a large external deficit and persistent inflation, with continued credit and house price growth.

"This does not bode well for a continued easing in monetary conditions," NBNZ said. That, together with planned spending increases by the centre-right coalition government, meant a continued hostile environment for both exports and investment.

The rise in business confidence was reflected across all sectors. In services, a net 25.9 percent of respondents expected conditions to improve, reversing the decline seen in December. For manufacturing, retailing, construction and agriculture the net figures were 7.1 percent, 15.3 percent, 19.7 percent and minus 11.0 percent, respectively.
NBNZ said the "dual economy" appeared alive and well.
"The outlook for agriculture and exports remains consistently the most pessimistic, while the domestic service sector leads the optimism.
"These sectoral differences hold across respondents' expected activity levels, profitability, and investment and employment intentions," it said.
Overall inflation expectations persisted at 2.75 percent for the year ahead, well above the 1.5 percent mid-point of the Reserve Bank's zero to three percent target range.
A net 11.8 percent of respondents aimed to raise prices over the next quarter, with the manufacturing sector at 16.6 percent, something NBNZ said would make the Reserve Bank wary.

A net 30.9 percent see interest rates continuing to fall, less convincing than the 65 percent in November. The outlook for profits remains weak, with only a net 10.4 percent expecting a rise. Only a net 6.2 percent expect to increase employment in the next year, with a net 15.4 percent in the service sector.
